data.gender_notes: Shivshankar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Shivshankar is a combination of two Sanskrit words: Shiva (the Hindu god of destruction and creation) and Shankar (the lord of the mountain). This name symbolizes the power and strength of Lord Shiva. The name Shivshankar carries the meaning “Shiva + Shankar (Lord of the Mountain)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Shivshankar usually hope their child will grow to embody shiva + shankar (lord of the mountain) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Shivshankar is a spiritual name that represents the power and strength of Lord Shiva. It is believed that this name brings blessings of prosperity, protection, and wisdom.
data.etymology: Shivshankar belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Shiva + Shankar (Lord of the Mountain).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shivshankar total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shivshankar holds significant cultural relevance in Hinduism. Shiva, the destructive and creative deity, is one of the most revered gods in Hinduism, and Shankar, representing the power and control over the natural world and human emotions, further strengthens this deity's significance. The name shares deep roots in Hindu mythology and is often used to denote strength, power, and faith. In Hindu communities, the name Shivshankar is a source of pride and is often passed on from generation to generation.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual standpoint, the name Shivshankar is deeply meaningful. Shiva, as a god, symbolizes the cycle of creation, preservation, and destruction, which is crucial for the world's continuous existence. Shankar, on the other hand, represents Lord Shiva's power and control over the natural world and human emotions. Together, the name Shivshankar signifies the attainment of spiritual enlightenment, the realization of the supreme self and the connection to the divine. It is believed that those who bear this name are blessed with the power and strength of Lord Shiva and are closer to attaining spiritual growth and self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shivshankar is a combination of two powerful Hindu deities, Shiva and Shankar. Shiva represents destruction and regeneration, while Shankar symbolizes peace and lord of the universe. Together, they embody the cycle of creation and destruction, representing the inherent duality of life.
